forecaster_note: Not looking like a standout day but there is some fun to decent sized waves around at south exposures. Clean here with northerly winds expected all day. Elsewhere around chest high but more lumpy and junky as some short period NE swell comes in. Surfable for now while winds are light but will become more unappealing as winds pick up later. Water temps will have cooled off from the NE winds we had yesterday and will have today. – Hugh McDowell, Surfline. Water temp is estimated (no live station feed this run).

wind.summary: NNW 8–9 km/h, offshore at dawn and cross-shore at Dee Why by 9am; swings NE 17–20 km/h onshore from 3pm.

shark.summary: 2 tagged white sharks detected at Palm Beach last night (5:49pm and 6:15pm), about 20 km north of Dee Why – nothing since, both now ~15h old. No detections at Dee Why, Long Reef, Curl Curl or Manly in the past 24h. Feed confirmed live: newest NSW detection 20 min ago, 119 statewide in 24h.

days.label: Today
days.note: 95 kJ mid-morning – well under your 450 floor, so this is a finesse morning, not a power one. Long Reef is the pick: waist–chest and offshore NNW right through midday. Dee Why goes cross-shore by 9am and the S 175° swell wraps soft there. NE onshore kills it from 3pm.

swells.label: Short-period NE windswell – adds the lump
S groundswell – wraps soft into Dee Why
Small ENE mid-period – best angle of the three

dee-why.window: Now until 9am while the NNW still has some offshore in it. Cross-shore after that, done by 3pm when the NE fills in.
alerts: S 175° swell wraps badly here – expect it noticeably softer than Long Reef or Curl Curl.
NNW turns cross-shore by 9am; NE 17–20 km/h onshore from 3pm.

tip.label: Frontside
tip.text: Point rights are your frontside wall – with only 2.5ft of 11s S wrapping in, sit wide and wait for the ENE sets rather than fighting the inside.

long-reef.window: Best of the four. Offshore NNW from dawn to midday – 10am–12pm on the pushing tide to the 10:02am high.

tip.label: Frontside
tip.text: The point rights run frontside for you. Cleanest wall of the four this morning – go here first.

curl-curl.window: Offshore NNW to midday. South end holds the S swell better – mid-morning peaks.

tip.label: Mixed
tip.text: Beachie peaks both ways. Take the rights off the south-end banks to stay frontside; the lefts are short into the NE lump.

manly.window: Cross-shore NNW from dawn – quick one only, and only if you're already down there.
alerts: Cross-shore all morning – bumpiest of the four.

tip.label: Mixed
tip.text: North Steyne peaks both ways. Rights keep you frontside, but the NE lump is closing the lefts out.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Small and clean early – 52 kJ, WSW offshore until about 10am, then SSE onshore from midday building to 30 km/h by dark. The real story is overnight: a 438 kJ S pulse lands Tuesday evening into Wednesday, but Wednesday is strong S'lies and messy.

dee-why.window: Dawn to 10am only. WSW offshore, then the SE change and it's finished.

long-reef.window: Early. WSW sits cross here – still clean enough before the SSE at midday.

curl-curl.window: WSW offshore till 10am, small peaky and clean. Blown out by afternoon.

manly.window: WSW offshore early – the protected corner holds longest once the SSE arrives.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Saturday is the day – 184 kJ with a 17s S groundswell and WNW offshore holding to midday. Long Reef chest–head, Curl Curl waist–shoulder. Sunday collapses: 12 kJ, knee-high, NNW. Plan Sat AM and don't bother Sunday. Consistency only 58% Saturday, so expect waits between sets.

dee-why.window: Sat 6am–12pm, WNW offshore. S 185° again wraps soft here – Sunday is knee-high, skip it.

long-reef.window: Sat 6am–12pm is the weekend's best window – chest to head, offshore WNW.

curl-curl.window: Sat morning, offshore WNW straight through to midday. Waist to shoulder.

manly.window: Smallest of the four both days – Sat AM or not at all.
